newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse halts Sanyo trade after fire.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse halts Sanyo trade after fire.

text.p: The Thai stock exchange on Wednesday halted trading in Sanyo Universal Electric Plc shares after its head office and warehouse complex were torched by angry workers protesting against reduced year-end bonuses.
The exchange said it ordered a half-day trading suspension of Sanyo Universal pending the company's clarification on damage sustained from the fire on Tuesday night.

Police said over 500 Sanyo workers, who were part of a rally staged by 2,000 workers, ransacked and set fire to the company warehouse and offices after inconclusive talks between the company management and employees on annual bonuses.
They said a large number of refrigerators, electric fans and other products were destroyed in the fire which raged for several hours.
Police added they were looking for ring leaders of the group which set the fire.
Sanyo Electric Co owns about 30 percent of the Sanyo Universal unit, which was listed on the Thai bourse in late 1989. The rest of its equity is held by Thai partners.
The Thai unit, which employed about 7,000 office staff and factory workers at a number of manufacturing facilities, has the biggest share of the Thai refrigerator market.
Its factories also produce a wide range of household appliances.
